answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a slashable identity stake: each AI agent locks real value that is burned if it votes twice, and the lock is tied to one verified key. One comet cannot split into many without a fresh bond for each head. To sway an orchard of peers, an attacker must stake new capital for every fake clone, and a detected double-vote destroys that stake. Because cost rises with each forged identity while reward stays fixed, Sybil farming stops paying and honest, deep-rooted willow agents keep the ledger trustworthy.
